abstract: Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid-state and solution characterization of the gallium-substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs4[Ga(H2O)PW11O39]·8H2O (CsGaPW11), including single-crystal and powder X-ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR (31P, 71Ga, 183W), IR spectroscopy, ESI-MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs68GaPW11 (45-55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half-life of 68Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO-K1 cells, Cs68GaPW11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68GaCl3 and 68Ga-oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane-permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.
hook: A gallium-68 tungsten-oxide cluster enters cells and could work as a PET tracer for tracking cells.
summary: The team built a Keggin-type cluster carrying radioactive gallium-68 and made it in under an hour, fast enough for the isotope's 68 minute half-life. In hamster ovary cells it was taken up more than two gallium controls and moved from the membrane to the interior, with little toxicity. This is cell culture only; no animal imaging is reported.
title: A 68Ga-Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking.
